Acquisition / Email delivery and engagement

Delivered-email unsubscribe rate

The percentage of delivered campaign recipient-message pairs associated with a confirmed campaign-attributed unsubscribe. This is a configured delivery-denominator measure reconstructed from delivery and subscription events.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of delivered campaign recipient-message pairs associated with a confirmed campaign-attributed unsubscribe. This is a configured delivery-denominator measure reconstructed from delivery and subscription events.

%

How we use it

We review audience fit, message frequency, and expectations so that subscriptions remain useful and preferences are respected.

Transparent calculationUnique delivered recipient-message pairs with a confirmed campaign-attributed unsubscribe / successfully delivered recipient-message pairs in the same observation window * 100
confirmed campaign unsubscribes24
delivered recipient messages4,800

24 / 4,800 * 100 = 0.5% delivered-email unsubscribe rate.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Audience source and consent history
  • Campaign topic
  • Frequency and recipient segment

Questions we investigate

  • Did expectations match the message received?
  • Is frequency concentrated on the same recipients?
  • Are attributed events confirmed rather than clicks?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Review preference and suppression handling.
  • Adjust segment relevance and message cadence.
  • Make subscription expectations clear at collection.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Lifecycle marketing lead
After each campaign window; monthly for frequency trends.

Required data

  • Successfully delivered campaign pairs
  • Confirmed unsubscribe events and attribution
  • Consent and suppression audit trail

Read the measure with context

Zero deliveries makes the rate undefined. Vendor native reports can use other denominators. A link click is not necessarily a completed unsubscribe; manual removals and unrelated preference changes need separate attribution.
